bug_semantics: Reflected XSS (CWE-79) in YaCyDefaultServlet.sendDirectory(): when dirAllowed directory listing is served, listing HTML is built with resource.getListHTML(base, ...). The listing base is URIUtil.addPaths(request.getRequestURI(), URIUtil.SLASH) rather than URIUtil.addEncodedPaths, so attacker-controlled request-URI characters are not kept encoded and are interpolated into generated hrefs. A client that requests a directory path containing HTML/JS metacharacters can therefore execute script in the directory-listing page. The same function also passed null instead of request.getQueryString() into the later 3-arg getListHTML API.
flaw_origin: The unencoded addPaths(request.getRequestURI()) + getListHTML(base, parent) directory-listing sink was first written when YaCyDefaultServlet was introduced on 2013-09-22 as a Jetty DefaultServlet-inspired servlet (4b77733e59dd8af742ff826c90c8d40b542b7563, source/net/yacy/http/YaCyDefaultServlet.java lines 494-496). Immediate parent 9619b8743c6d1cf6d2ea110b52e3819d6ec9b478 has no YaCyDefaultServlet and no addPaths(request.getRequestURI()) call. Later 20b48f894fad200ae90a67aba753a616020df051 (package move), 7947baeb49b9f6df4195baf8e6b1dcaa771f734f (Jetty 3-arg getListHTML(..., null)), and 48fcf3b3b5b8d2f44363367840c3f1ebdbdd3634 (final/this restyle) only moved or restyled the same mechanism and are not BICs.

reasoning: CVE-2026-24824 is a published CWE-79 advisory, not withdrawn. The concrete sink is sendDirectory() directory-listing HTML that embeds a base URI built with Jetty URIUtil.addPaths on request.getRequestURI(), which does not preserve encoding the way addEncodedPaths does; getListHTML then emits that base into listing markup. The smallest public first-write of that mechanism is 4b77733e59dd8af742ff826c90c8d40b542b7563 (new file YaCyDefaultServlet.java, 2013-09-22). The immediate parent exists and lacks both the file and the addPaths(request.getRequestURI()) call, so this is not a move/squash/revert BIC. Later blame hits (7947baeb49 3-arg API; 48fcf3b3b5 final) restyle the same call and are excluded. The BIC is an ancestor of CVE-listed Release_1.92 and of the 2025-09-14 fix; the merge 008b8c3b499ef993a755b0688d9742df9c203535 (direct fd6a2bb9439f5b005ab8e362ba02e32fd6b374dc) is first present in Release_1.941.
